summary: Media details airing information can become inconsistent across top-level navigation stacks because details are fetched once when a retained MediaDetailsViewModel is created, while a separate stack can create a fresh detail instance. PR #16 hardens newly executed detail queries with NetworkFirst but does not itself refresh an already-retained ViewModel.

facts.value: The same anime was reported with stale episode/next-airing data through a normal entry path and correct data when opened through Calendar. Calendar does not pass episode state into MediaDetails, it navigates with the same media ID route.
NavActionManager.toMediaDetails(id) creates only Route.MediaDetails(id). Navigator appends non-top-level routes to the currently selected top-level back stack.

NavigationState creates a separate NavBackStack for every top-level route, decorates every stack with a ViewModelStore NavEntry decorator, and explicitly retains state even when a top-level route is not currently in use.

MediaDetailsViewModel starts getMediaDetails() only from init. MediaDetailsView obtains the ViewModel from the NavEntry-scoped Koin ViewModelStore and there is no general visibility/resume refresh path for the details query.

Before PR #16, MediaRepository.getMediaDetails() did not specify a freshness override. PR #16 adds FetchPolicy.NetworkFirst so newly executed MediaDetails queries prefer current network data and fall back to cache on network failure.

Two freshness mechanisms are proven to exist: a previously cache-first detail query path and retained per-top-level MediaDetails ViewModel state. The physical reproduction needed to attribute the original symptom to one mechanism or both is still missing.
PR #16 head 38ee924472aa95f61b9c56e65a9c362f3b37eb7c passed Android CI run 32909362215 and Temporary Performance APK run 32909362197. Artifact 9586206324 belongs to that exact head.

constraints: Do not describe retained ViewModel state as the sole proven root cause until a reproducible test or physical run distinguishes it from the Apollo freshness path.
Do not disable Apollo caching globally.
Do not delete or collapse the separate top-level back stacks merely to force MediaDetails recreation.
Any retained-state fix should refresh only when useful and avoid permanent background or recomposition-driven network requests.
Keep this issue distinct from issue.aniworld-repository-gap: fresher AniList data is not proof of German AniWorld availability.
